name: Mellah
hero_subtitle: Lanes and memory of the Jewish community inside the walls.

overview.title: A quarter of memory inside the citadel
overview.p1: After the Portuguese left, a Jewish community settled inside the walls of El Jadida. The mellah still shows the layout of that era: narrow lanes, modest façades and a few remaining traces of synagogues.
overview.p2: Walking through it adds a human and historical layer to the visit of the Portuguese City, beyond the military architecture.
overview.p3: The quarter is lived-in and quiet. Respect residents and combine the stroll with the nearby cistern and church.

q1.question: How much time for Mellah?
q1.answer: 30 to 60 minutes is usually enough for a good visit.

q2.question: Is there an entry fee?
q2.answer: Many outdoor areas are free; the cistern has a ticket. Check on site.

q3.question: Can I visit with children?
q3.answer: Yes, most sites are suitable for families with basic supervision.

q4.question: Is it open every day?
q4.answer: Outdoor sites are generally accessible daily; indoor sites may close one day a week.

q5.question: Do I need a guide?
q5.answer: Not required, but a local guide enriches the history of the Portuguese City.
